# Generator-shortcuts answer

The strongest plausible shortcut is:

> Complete a same-colour adjacent diagonal only when both of the other corners of its 2×2 box are zero.

This is essentially the baseline generator’s old domain restriction. It fits all three canonical demonstrations, because every demonstrated target pair is isolated and has empty companion corners. It is stronger and more plausible than a purely positional shortcut because it agrees with the visible geometric rule everywhere the demonstrations exercise it.

An exact disagreement input is:

```text
2 3
0 2
```

The colour-2 cells are opposite corners of the only 2×2 box. The intended rule overwrites the occupied colour-3 companion and returns:

```text
2 2
2 2
```

The shortcut refuses to act because one companion corner is nonzero, leaving:

```text
2 3
0 2
```

I checked the intended output with the supported selected Racket authority command. Its source-bound report is `checks/counterexample/b37eb391ddc0/racket.json`; the input and rival output are retained beside it in `input.json` and `rival.json`. The report records generator SHA-256 `c113fd93cc524873595b4bf9808b87727c97548f68c0a7427424c782e393b47f`, executed rule hash `24318a9ceacd`, input hash `4b6f15f6…`, and output hash `a0a73a8f…`. The same case is a task-local regression test and appears in the real-Racket reference probe.

Yes, the proposed generator emits such cases deliberately. In `checks/reference-probe.json`, every one of 300 final-source samples—100 per difficulty band—contains an occupied-companion witness and disagrees with both `isolated_pairs_only` and `preserve_occupied`. This is a measured finite sample, not a claim that no other shortcut exists.
